problem: The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=t{e}^{-2t}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x.$

feedback.problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29},$ where $t>0$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x.$

$t\in (${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of increasing $x,$ then its velocity is positive. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29}) \\  & =\frac{10t-20}{2\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29}} \\  & =\frac{10(t-2)}{2\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29}} \\  & =\frac{5(t-2)}{\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29}}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x$, we solve $v(t)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & >0 \\ \frac{5(t-2)}{\sqrt{5{t}^{2}-20t+29}} & >0 \\ 5(t-2) & >0 \\ t-2 & >0 \\ t & >2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of increasing $x$ is 

$$
t\in (2,\infty ).
$$
